fix_commit_message:
avcodec/jpeg2000dec: fix integer overflow in dequantization_int_97()

Fixes: signed integer overflow: 2147483640 + 32 cannot be represented in type 'int'
Fixes: 473569764/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_AV_CODEC_ID_JPEG2000_DEC_fuzzer-5377306970619904

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix fa2aec73ed8f on top of intro 82467b635efc via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): The JPEG2000 decoder's dequantization_int_97() function, used for the reversible/lossless (integer 9-7-like) wavelet dequantization path, performs a rounding addition on a decoded wavelet coefficient before right-shifting it by a fixed PRESCALE amount. The addition `val + (1 << (PRESCALE - 1))` is performed entirely in 32-bit signed int arithmetic. Because `val` can approach INT32_MAX after the sign-magnitude to two's-complement conversion (from a maliciously crafted or corrupted JPEG2000 codestream), adding even a small constant (32 when PRESCALE=6) can overflow the 32-bit signed integer range, which is undefined behavior in C and was caught by fuzzing (OSS-Fuzz/UBSan). Root cause: The rounding-bias addition prior to the right shift in dequantization_int_97() was implemented using 32-bit `int` arithmetic without accounting for the fact that decoded coefficient magnitudes can be close to INT32_MAX, causing the addition of the rounding constant to overflow a signed 32-bit integer.
